subject: Decision Making
title: Monte Carlo Simulations
description: A short lesson to help you apply Monte Carlo Simulations.

hook.text: Monte Carlo simulations run a decision thousands of times with random inputs to map the range of possible outcomes.

buildup.text: Named after the casino, these simulations were invented for nuclear weapons research at Los Alamos in the 1940s.

discovery.text: Instead of one prediction, you get a distribution. You see best case, worst case, and everything in between.

twist.text: Monte Carlo revealed that humans wildly underestimate tail risks. The unlikely happens more than intuition expects.

climax.text: Monte Carlo thinking replaced point estimates with ranges. Better to be roughly right than precisely wrong.

punchline.text: Run it a thousand times. Monte Carlo maps what could happen.

quiz.question: What do Monte Carlo simulations produce?
options: A range of possible outcomes with probabilities
